raw_response:
I’m 76 this year, and I’ve been working this land for 50 years. Didn’t get much schooling—just a few years of primary school—but I know my fields. My farm is 16.1 mu, wheat-maize double crop, same as most folks around here. My son works in a factory in town, so it’s mainly me and my wife in the fields now, though he comes back when he can for the busy times. We have a little money from his wages, but I still watch every yuan. At my age, I don’t try new tricks. What worked last year is what I do this year.

**Wheat:** I plant right after we finish the maize harvest, usually around the 8th to 12th of October. I use an improved variety I’ve been growing for three years now. I buy fresh seed every second or third year—this year I saved seed from last autumn, so that saves a bit of money. Before planting, I spread about 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu and run the rotary tiller. That’s my base. Come spring, when the wheat greens up, I look at the color. If it’s a bit yellow—last year it was—I topdress with another 20 jin or so of urea at jointing. If it looks green and strong, maybe I do a little less, but I’d rather put a bit too much than too little. I irrigate three times: once before winter so the wheat can survive the cold, once in March at jointing, and once in April or May when the grain is filling. Pumping costs money—about 25 yuan each time—but without water you get nothing. I spray herbicide in spring for the weeds, and if I see disease on the leaves like two years ago, I’ll add fungicide.

**Maize:** As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, we plant maize. The window is tight, sometimes less than a week, so there’s no time for deep plowing. I chop the wheat straw and rotary till, then plant right away. I always buy hybrid seed—can’t save it, it doesn’t work next year. One bag covers about 2 mu, costs around 100 yuan. I put fertilizer in the row at planting, about 40 jin of compound per mu. If July is dry, I irrigate once when the maize is jointing, and maybe once more in August if it doesn’t rain. Usually twice is enough. I spray herbicide at planting, and if I see corn borer like last year, I’ll spray insecticide too.

**Labor and money:** Me and my wife do most of the daily work, but for planting and harvest we need extra hands. I’m old now—I can’t lift bags like I used to. We hire a few days of labor each season, maybe seven days across the whole year. My son helps when he’s back. Total costs for seed, fertilizer, water, pesticide, and hired help will be around 9,800 yuan this year. That’s a lot for us, but we have some cash from my son’s off-farm job, so we can manage. I expect about 450 kg per mu for wheat and 480 kg per mu for maize if the weather is normal. Not going to get rich, but we’ll eat and have some left over.
